overview: CS4101 is the first Capstone maneuver-and-EP flight. The discussion should show that the student can brief prior maneuvers by setup, contract, and discontinue criteria, then apply emergency procedures with N/W/C judgment and a practical recovery plan.

studyNotes.headline: Discussion Items

items.text: Any previously discussed maneuver means the instructor can sample across FAM, Formation, Instrument, and VNAV-style skills; answer with an organized method instead of trying to recite the whole syllabus.

children.text: Start with the maneuver purpose, entry setup, configuration, airspeed, altitude or area requirement, and clear-area or formation contract.
State the execution flow, maneuver-complete cue, and the reason you would discontinue, terminate, or knock-it-off.
Connect the maneuver to the capstone profile: formation work, high work, instrument approach, missed approach, holding, divert, or recovery.
For FAM maneuvers, keep trim, coordination, stall/OCF awareness, energy state, and recovery altitude in the answer.
For formation maneuvers, brief who owns deconfliction, what visual reference matters, and when Wing must call lost sight, blind, terminate, or knock-it-off.
For instrument work, brief setup, clearance or route logic, scan priorities, configuration timing, missed-approach plan, and lost-comm assumptions.
For navigation or VNAV-style tasks, brief route verification, fuel/time awareness, weather, airspace, and how the plan changes if the profile no longer matches the day.
Do not memorize local profile names as the procedure. Use current 1801, SOP, IFG, weather, fuel, and day-of brief to decide which procedure applies.
If a maneuver answer depends on local routing, frequency, runway flow, or holding fix, say that it must be verified from the current local source.

items.text: Any emergency procedure means the student must show a repeatable decision flow: cue, aircraft control, memory item, checklist or N/W/C, and recovery choice.

children.text: Aviate first: maintain control, establish the correct attitude and airspeed, and protect altitude, terrain clearance, and formation separation.
Analyze the cue and execute any required critical action memory items.
Use the checklist and N/W/Cs to decide whether the branch is continue, recover, PEL, forced landing, section support, divert, or eject.
Communicate intentions to the other aircraft, ATC, or support agency when the aircraft is stable enough.
For single-ship EPs, brief recognition, immediate actions, minimum controllable or glide numbers, and the field or ejection decision point.
For formation EPs, brief lead transfer, perch, detach, lost sight or blind separation, and who coordinates with ATC.
For IMC EPs, prioritize instrument scan, safe altitude, clearance or emergency authority, and lost-comm plan.
For divert or damaged-aircraft cases, brief suitable field selection, fuel, weather, runway, crash crew, and whether the flight should remain joined.
Do not invent an exhaustive EP list for the event. Use the published EP/N/W/C source for verbatim items and be ready to apply them to the profile.
When the emergency conflicts with the original mission plan, the recovery plan wins.

items.text: Any Previously Discussed Maneuver and Any Emergency Procedure

studyNotes.summary: CS4101 should be studied as a cumulative flight brief: use a consistent maneuver answer format and a disciplined EP decision flow instead of trying to memorize every possible prompt.

summary: CS4101 covers cumulative maneuver review and emergency-procedure decision flow for the first Capstone flight.
